topics.title: World Happiness Report
bullets: Oxford Wellbeing Research Centre has published the World Happiness Report of 2026. Total of 147 countries featured.
It was published in collaboration with Gallup and UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network.
The report was released on the March 20 on the occasion of International Happiness Day. @CLAT_OWNER About the Report –

Since 2024, the report has been published by the Wellbeing Research Centre at the University of Oxford, in partnership with Gallup, the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network, and an independent editorial board.
The editorial board consists of the three founding editors, John F. Helliwell, Richard Layard, and Jeffrey D. Sachs, along with Jan-Emmanuel De Neve, Lara Aknin, and Shun Wang.
The report primarily uses data from the Gallup World Poll. @CLAT_OWNER
Top 5 Happiest Countries: Finland > Iceland > Denmark > Cosata Rica > Sweden. Finland has been ranked 1st for the fifth time.
Unhappy Countries: Afghanistan, Sierra Leone, Malawi, and, Zimbabwe.
India improved its ranking to 116th in 2026 from 118th in 2025. @CLAT_OWNER
India performs lower compared to some neighbouring countries like China (65), Pakistan (104) and Nepal (99). However, it ranks above countries like Bangladesh (127) and Sri Lanka (134).
The report shows declining happiness in Western countries and rising levels in Eastern Europe.
The concept of Gross National Happiness is officially followed by Bhutan as their main development indicator. @CLAT_OWNER
Afghanistan remains the unhappiest country globally (147th), followed by Sierra Leone (146th) and Malawi (145th).
Costa Rica has performed well, rising to 4th place from 23rd in 2023 while Israel ranked 8th. The United States is at 23rd place, Canada is at 25th and Britain at 29th. @CLAT_OWNER
It asks people to rate their life on a 0-10 scale, from the worst possible life (0) to the best possible life (10).
Country rankings were based on answers given by around 100,000 people in 140 countries and territories who were asked to rate their own lives.
Factors for evaluation of happiness ranking: GDP per capita; Life expectancy; Social support; Freedom to make life choices; Generosity; and Perceptions of corruption. @CLAT_OWNER
The Gallup World Poll questionnaire measures 14 areas within its core questions:
(1) business & economic,
(2) citizen engagement,
(3) communications & technology,
(4) diversity (social issues),
(5) education & families,
(6) emotions (well-being),
(7) environment & energy,
(8) food & shelter,
(9) government and politics,
(10) law & order (safety)
(11) health,
(12) religion & ethics,
(13) transportation, and
(14) work. @CLAT_OWNER
The “Goldilocks” idea in social media suggests that limited usage - roughly under an hour per day - can be more beneficial for mental well-being than not using it at all.
Current global usage averages about 2.5 hours daily.

Passive, visual platforms like Instagram and TikTok promote social comparison, while communication apps like WhatsApp and Facebook are associated with higher life satisfaction, especially in Latin America and the Middle East. @CLAT_OWNER History –
In July 2011, the United Nations General Assembly adopted resolution 65/309, also named as Happiness: Towards a Holistic Definition of Development.
The first World Happiness Report was released on 1 April 2012, as a foundational text for the UN High Level Meeting - Well-being and Happiness: Defining a New Economic Paradigm.
On 2 April 2012, this was followed by the first UN High Level Meeting called Wellbeing and Happiness: Defining a New Economic Paradigm. @CLAT_OWNER
The meeting was chaired by UN Secretary General Ban Ki-Moon, in addition to that prime minister Jigme Thinley of Bhutan.
The first report outlined the state of world happiness, causes of happiness and misery, and policy implications highlighted by case studies.
In 2013, the second World Happiness Report was issued, and in 2015 the third. Since 2016, it has been issued on an annual basis on 20 March, to coincide with the UN's International Day of Happiness.
Theme 2026: “Caring and Sharing” – continued focus on empathy, social connection, and collective happiness. @CLAT_OWNER The Report Highlights for India –
Several structural issues affect India’s ranking, including income inequality, unemployment, and access to basic services.
Rural-urban disparities also play a significant role.
Perception of corruption and limited freedom in life choices further impact life satisfaction. @CLAT_OWNER
Themes across years:
2024: “Happiness Together” – focused on connection, belonging, and shared well-being.
2025: “Caring and Sharing” – emphasized kindness, generosity, and community bonds. @CLAT_OWNER Sustainable Development Network –
The Sustainable Development Network (SDSN) is an NGO setup by the United Nations in 2012. It was initiated by then UN Secretary- General Ban Ki-moon.
It has been advocating for sustainable development solutions, such as the implementation of the Paris Climate Agreement and the Sustainable Development Goals, since 2012.
The network's objectives are to combine approaches to economic, social, and environmental concerns and to accelerate collaborative learning. @CLAT_OWNER
It collaborates closely with the commercial sector, civil society, international finance organizations, and UN agencies.
The group wants to include leaders in the network's development from a variety of backgrounds and geographical areas.
Paris, Delhi, and New York are the locations of SDSN's offices. @CLAT_OWNER Gallup –
Gallup, Inc. is an American multinational analytics and advisory company based in Washington, D.C.
It was founded by George Gallup in 1935.
The company became known for conducting public opinion polls worldwide. @CLAT_OWNER

topics.title: Lipulekh Pass
bullets: India-China border trade via Lipulekh Pass will resume in June 2026 after a 7-year pause. The trading window is expected to run from June to September, with a possible extension depending on weather conditions.
The move boosts local economy, strengthens diplomatic ties, and revives historic Himalayan trade routes in Uttarakhand’s Pithoragarh district.
Lipulekh Pass is ocated in Uttarakhand’s Pithoragarh district. IAS Ashish Bhatgai is the District Magistrate of Pithorgarh district. @CLAT_OWNER
The decision come after important discussions between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese counterpart Foreign Minister Wang Yi in August 2025.
Both sides agreed to restore multiple trade points, including, Lipulekh Pass (Uttarakhand) Shipki La (Himachal Pradesh) Nathu La (Sikkim).
India first started trade through Lipulekh Pass in 1954 with China. @CLAT_OWNER About Lipulekh Pass –
Lipulekh Pass is a high-altitude mountain pass situated in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, near the trijunction of India, Nepal, and China.
It connects India with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
Located at an elevation of approximately 5,334 metres or around 17,500 feet, the pass serves as a critical gateway to the higher Himalayas. @CLAT_OWNER
After the 1962 Sino-Indian War, the route was closed for several decades due to security concerns. It was reopened in 1992 for limited border trade between India and China.
Subsequently, other passes such as Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh (1994) and Nathu La in Sikkim (2006) were also opened to promote cross-border trade.
It serves as a major route for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, a revered pilgrimage for Hindus, Buddhists, and Jains. @CLAT_OWNER
It is accessible from the Indian side via the town of Dharchula.
Border trade with Tibet via the Lipulekh had resumed in 1992 after a long suspension. However, it was halted in 2019 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
It is near the Tibetan trading town of Taklakot (Purang). @CLAT_OWNER
It also plays a vital role in sustaining the livelihoods of border communities, particularly the Bhotiya tribes, who have historically depended on trans-Himalayan trade.
The Lipulekh Pass is known as Pulang-Gunji in the local Tibetan dialect. It is one of three villages located in the Kalapani area.
Though currently under Indian control, Nepal has consistently asserted its claim over the area. @CLAT_OWNER Nepal’s Claim –
Nepal has previously protested India and China making bilateral arrangements over Lipulekh, in 2015 and 2020.
The outgoing prime minister of Nepal, Sushila Karki, as well as the incoming Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) government is sought to raise this issue with both India and China.
It was also incorporated into Nepal’s official map in 2020 through an amendment to the constitution. @CLAT_OWNER
Nepal claims the southern side of the pass called Kalapani territory, based on the Treaty of Sugauli 1816 between British East India Company and Nepal.
The treaty delimited the boundary along Kali river (Sharda/Mahakali river). It stated that Nepal would cede the territories west of the Kali river.
Nepal claims that the Kali river originates from Limpiyadhura, west of Kalapani and Lipulekh. @CLAT_OWNER
On this basis, Nepal claims Kalapani, Lipulekh, and Limpiyadhura as its part.
India claims that the Kali river originates at Kalapani village in Pithoragarh, where all its tributaries merge.
Hence, the bone of contention is the differing interpretation of the origin of the Kali River. @CLAT_OWNER Source: Wiley Library @CLAT_OWNER Importance for India –
The pass holds significant strategic military importance, allowing for faster troop movement along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China.
India constructed a road to the pass in 2020 to improve access for pilgrims and traders, which intensified the diplomatic tensions with Nepal.
It is a part of Bharat Rannbhoomi Darshan (battlefield tourism initiative). @CLAT_OWNER
It provides India with direct access to the Tibetan plateau, making it vital for surveillance, troop movement, and border management along the India–China frontier.
The pass is actively monitored by forces like the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), helping India keep track of Chinese activities across the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
Road connectivity up to Lipulekh improves rapid mobilization of troops, supplies, and equipment in high-altitude areas. @CLAT_OWNER

topics.title: Pearl Harbor Attack
bullets: On March 20, in a Press Conference in USA with the Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, President Donald Trump made a joke about the Pearl Harbor Attack.
President Trump was asked why he did not give Japan and other allies any notice of the US-Israeli attack on Iran, Trump responded, with Takaichi by his side at the Oval Office:
“We wanted surprise. Who knows better about surprise than Japan, OK? Why didn’t you tell me about Pearl Harbor, OK? Right?” @CLAT_OWNER Pearl Harbour Attack –
On December 7, 1941, about 180 aircraft of the Imperial Japanese Navy attacked the US Naval base at Pearl Harbour on the island of Oahu in Hawaii.
The bombing killed over 2,300 Americans, and destroyed the battleships USS Arizona and USS Oklahoma.
Roughly 160 aircraft were destroyed, and 150 were damaged. @CLAT_OWNER
At that time the US President was Franklin D. Roosevelt.
Three days later of the Pearl Harbor Attack Japan’s allies Germany and Italy declared war on the United States.
Congress responded by declaring war on them as well. With that, the United States officially entered World War II, fighting in both Europe and the Pacific. @CLAT_OWNER
Japan attacked Pearl Harbor largely because of growing tensions with the United States.
In 1910, Japan annexed Korea and, in 1937, it invaded China, sending alarm bells ringing in the US and other Western powers about Japan’s manifest expansionist agenda.

Between December 1937 and January 1938, an episode which is referred to as the “Nanking Massacre” or the “Rape of Nanking”, occurred — Japanese soldiers killed and raped Chinese civilians and combatants. @CLAT_OWNER
The US was against Japan’s aggression in China, and imposed economic sanctions and trade embargoes after its invasion.
Japan was reliant on imports for oil and other natural resources — this was one of the reasons why it invaded China, and later French Indo-China (present day Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia).
In the summer of 1941, the United States cut off oil exports to Japan in response to Japan’s expansion in Asia. @CLAT_OWNER
By attacking Pearl Harbor, Japanese leaders hoped to destroy the U.S. Pacific Fleet and prevent the United States from interfering in Japan’s plans in Asia.
But the Pearl Harbor attack had failed in its objective to completely destroy the Pacific Fleet. However, it destroyed battleships like USS Arizona and USS Oklahoma.
The Japanese bombers missed oil tanks, ammunition sites and repair facilities, and not a single U.S. aircraft carrier was present during the attack. @CLAT_OWNER
Currently, the Pearl Harbour is home to the USS Arizona memorial, the Battleship Missouri, and the Pacific Aviation Museum.
It is also a working Joint Naval and Air Force Base. In 2010, Pearl Harbour was combined with Hickam Air Force Base to create the Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam.

In 2016, then US President Barack Obama and the late Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe visited Pearl Harbour in a gesture of reconciliation. @CLAT_OWNER Source: Insight IAS @CLAT_OWNER Aftermath of Pearl Harbor –
The Doolittle Raid in April 1942 was the first U.S. air strike on Tokyo, boosting American morale.
The Battle of Midway (June 1942) was the turning point, where the U.S. sank four Japanese aircraft carriers.

The Battle of Leyte Gulf in 1944 was the largest naval battle in history and crippled the Japanese Navy. U.S. forces captured Iwo Jima and Okinawa in 1945 to gain a staging ground for a mainland invasion. @CLAT_OWNER

General Curtis LeMay shifted tactics to low-altitude incendiary (fire) bombing of Japanese cities. The Firebombing of Tokyo (March 9–10, 1945) killed an estimated 100,000 people and destroyed 16 square miles.
The Manhattan Project developed the world's first atomic weapons in secret.
On August 6, 1945, the B-29 Enola Gay dropped the "Little Boy" atomic bomb on Hiroshima. On August 9, 1945, the B-29 Bockscar dropped the "Fat Man" atomic bomb on Nagasaki. @CLAT_OWNER
The Soviet Union declared war on Japan on August 8, 1945, further pressuring the Japanese leadership.
Japan announced its surrender on August 15, 1945 (V-J Day). The formal surrender was signed on September 2, 1945, aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay.

The U.S. military occupied Japan until 1952 to oversee its transition to a democracy. Total Japanese casualties from the U.S. campaign exceeded 2.5 million, including roughly 800,000 civilians. @CLAT_OWNER Post Hiroshima-Nagasaki –
Partial Test Ban Treaty (1963): Bans nuclear tests in the atmosphere, in outer space, and under water.
Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) (1970): To prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and weapons technology, etc.
Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (1996): Bans all nuclear test explosions, whether for military or civilian purposes. @CLAT_OWNER
United Nations Office of Disarmament Affairs: It aims for general and complete disarmament globally.
Others: Pact for the Future, Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, etc.
International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) was established in 1957 for international cooperation on civilian nuclear research. @CLAT_OWNER World War II –
It was a war during the years 1939-45.
The principal belligerents were the Axis powers — Germany, Italy, and Japan — and the Allies — France, Great Britain, the United States, the Soviet Union, and, to a lesser extent, China.

It was the biggest conflict in history that had lasted almost six years. Nearly some 100 million people had been militarised, and 50 million had been killed (around 3% of the world's population). @CLAT_OWNER

The major causes include the impact of the Treaty of Versailles following WWI, the worldwide economic depression, failure of appeasement, the rise of militarism in Germany and Japan, and the failure of the League of Nations.
Following World War I, Germany was forced to sign the Treaty of Versailles. Under this treaty, Germany had to accept guilt for the war and to pay reparations.
Germany lost territory and was prohibited from having a large military. The humiliation faced by Germany under this treaty, paved the way for the spread of Ultra-Nationalism in Germany. @CLAT_OWNER
The German invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939 and subsequently two days later, Britain and France declared war on Germany.
September 03, 1939 marked the beginning of World War II.
Germany initially achieved rapid victories using Blitzkrieg (lightning war), quickly conquering Poland, Denmark, Norway, Belgium, and France by 1940. @CLAT_OWNER
The Battle of Britain marked the first major defeat of Germany, where the UK successfully resisted sustained aerial bombardment.
In 1941, Germany launched Operation Barbarossa, opening the Eastern Front and turning the conflict into a massive war of attrition.
Japan’s surprise Attack on Pearl Harbor brought the United States formally into the war, globalising the conflict further. @CLAT_OWNER
The Battle of Stalingrad became a decisive turning point, as German forces suffered a catastrophic defeat against the Soviet Union.
In Western Europe, the Allies launched the D-Day, leading to the liberation of Nazi-occupied territories.
The Nazi regime carried out the Holocaust, a systematic genocide in which around six million Jews and millions of others were killed in concentration and extermination camps. @CLAT_OWNER
By April 1945, Adolf Hitler committed suicide as Allied forces closed in, and Germany surrendered in May 1945.
In the Pacific theatre, the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, leading to Japan’s surrender shortly thereafter.
The war resulted in an estimated 70–85 million deaths, including both military personnel and civilians, making it the deadliest conflict in human history. @CLAT_OWNER
The aftermath led to the creation of the United Nations to promote international peace and cooperation.
It also marked the beginning of the Cold War, as tensions grew between the United States and the Soviet Union.
India contributed significantly, with over 2.5 million soldiers serving under British command in various theatres, making it one of the largest volunteer forces in the war. @CLAT_OWNER
